checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The opening does seduce with sensory texture ('the smell of a field right after a deep-till pass,' the hull 'warm... deep warm, the kind that comes from inside') and the Pip-mourning scene has genuine strange-beauty, but for long stretches (the drone battles, the CJ/Hauser procedural scenes, the checkpoint negotiation) the prose shifts into functional thriller-mechanics mode where observation and plot-logistics dominate over allure — the horror (a man's death, drone kills) lands amid mostly procedural describing rather than being preceded by seduction specific to that moment.
checks.Fix: Slow down and sensualize the mid-story machine-violence and procedural beats (the drone kills, the man's death, the checkpoint exchange) with the same lush, strange-beautiful texture given to the opening and the burial scene, so allure precedes every horror beat, not just the first one.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The story opens directly with an inciting incident (a wrongness sound pulling Wes from bed) rather than a grounded, unremarkable entry beat; within the first few paragraphs we're already at the dead machine, tool marks, and a mystery, with no prior moment of ordinary world-functioning to earn the seduction first.
checks.Fix: Precede the wail with a short beat of Wes doing an ordinary morning task around the living machine — checking a gauge, watching it till a row, something mundane that shows the world working normally — before the wrongness interrupts it.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: CorpoNations/Eigenlift towers and neuretics are glossed lightly and in-voice ('too young for the mesh' for neuretics; 'thirty stories each, rising straight out of the corn with no town around them' for Eigenlift towers), but some proprietary terms like 'ArcSec,' 'Zone-12,' 'GLMZ run,' and 'Crown' (for the machine's dome) are used repeatedly with zero orientation, forcing a first-time reader to infer meaning entirely from context over many paragraphs.
checks.Fix: Add one brief in-voice touch when 'Zone-12,' 'ArcSec,' or 'Crown' first appears—e.g., have CJ's POV register ArcSec as 'the only badge this corridor had had in a hundred years' (already present) but do similarly for 'Zone-12 boundary' and clarify 'Crown' as the machine's platform the first time Wes climbs onto it.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: "South meant deeper into the Zone — the Great Lakes corridor, more buyers, fewer questions" is offered as gloss for 'the GLMZ run,' but the acronym 'GLMZ' itself appears bare in that same sentence and is never expanded into its literal full term before or after use.
checks.Fix: Replace 'the GLMZ run' with something like 'the Great Lakes Multi-Zone run, GLMZ, deeper into the Zone corridor' so the full term precedes the acronym in-voice.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: "He didn't look at her. 'Lord Long Legs.' / She looked at him. / 'I was five,' he said." — a single, unguarded flash of the child Wes once was, immediately followed by his return to competent, unbothered self as he declines the ride and says he'll walk.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The node lands multiple resolutions (module buried, machine departs, Pip urinates on the patch, Wes names it 'Lord Long Legs') and then closes on 'I'll walk,' which reads as a hopeful/settled character beat rather than a quiet gesture that adds cost or dread; the final exchange is almost warm/whimsical, undercutting the 'holding the cost' effect.
checks.Fix: Cut or dampen the naming exchange and end instead on a single unresolved image (e.g., the sealed asphalt scar, or Wes's silence at the horizon) that carries unease about what the buried module means and what 'this city/corridor' will do next, without supplying an origin-story punchline like the dog's territorial joke.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The first-pass story is complete and legible as a boy-and-machine chase narrative, but details like the machine warming and slowing its rhythm when Wes rests on it, Pip's ritualized 'mourning' sit, the burial tamping described in the same procedural language as planting, and the final name 'Lord Long Legs' (revealed only at the very end to be a childhood nickname) all reread differently once the reader knows the machine grieves and Wes has known it since age five.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The story builds its universe (Behemoths, Eigenlift towers, ArcSec, Zone boundaries) entirely through in-scene action and Wes/CJ's grounded sensory experience rather than expository dumps; terms like 'kill-switch protocol' or 'Zone-12 boundary' arrive embedded in dialogue and alert boards that a first-time reader can parse contextually, while the emotional core (a machine mourning, a boy bonding with it, a dog's loyalty) needs no prior universe knowledge to land.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: CorpoNations (Eigenlift, ArcSec, Arcturus), nanites-as-Behemoths, and a systemic gray-zone economy (scavs, Nzambe, GLMZ run) are all richly textured, and the Behemoth is clearly an agent with stakes, not a tool. But the Schism is never mentioned or implied at all, and neuretics appear only glancingly ('No neuretics — too young for the mesh') without establishing what they do or the social/economic divide they create.
checks.Fix: Add a beat where CJ's augmented reaction speed or cognitive load is contrasted against Wes's unaugmented perception, and weave in at least one concrete reference to the Schism as the historical rupture that shaped this world (e.g., why Behemoths exist, why the Zones are gray, or why the land looks the way it does).
